title: Latency-targeted preemptive batcher and fairness policy for continuous batching
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Continuous batching improves GPU throughput by aggregating tokens across requests, but when latency-sensitive requests arrive we need a principled, low-overhead way to preempt in-progress batches without regressing throughput or causing KV cache thrash. Current heuristics can starve low-priority tenants or cause large KV cache evictions that increase cold token cost.

Goal: Design and implement a latency-targeted preemptive batch scheduler that enforces per-request SLOs (latency targets) while preserving fairness and minimizing GPU memory churn. The system should integrate with KV cache management to avoid heavy cache eviction on preemption and support graceful partial execution/resumption of model contexts where possible.

Scope: This ticket covers the scheduler policy, KV cache eviction strategy changes needed for preemption, memory accounting updates to allow transient overcommit detection, and a first-pass rollout on dedicated capacity nodes behind an opt-in runtime flag. It excludes model kernel changes and long-lived multi-tenant accounting (will follow in ENG-9750).
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler enforces per-request latency target for prioritized buckets and reduces p95 tail for latency-sensitive class by >= 30% under mixed load compared to baseline
No more than 10% relative throughput loss for best-effort workloads under representative traffic patterns (measured by tokens/sec)
KV cache hit-rate degradation <= 5% at steady-state; cache churn metric shows bounded eviction spike within 30s of preemption events
GPU memory fragmentation/reclaimed memory metrics show < 5% additional overhead compared to baseline during preemption-heavy workloads
Automated integration test simulating preemption across 1000 concurrent sessions passes (functional correctness: no corrupted KV state, resumption works where applicable)
Feature gated and can be disabled at node or account level; rollout plan documented and smoke-tested in staging
implementation_notes: Scheduler model: maintain three logical priority lanes (latency, balanced, best-effort). Each incoming request carries a target_latency_ms and priority token. Scheduler attempts to include request in current active batch if target_latency_ms >= remaining_batch_hold_ms else triggers preemption path.

Preemption semantics: preempt by splitting the active batch into two execution slices — commit state for latency lane requests first, then resume or continue remainder. If model/kernel doesn't support slice resume, run a fast-path single-request execution for latency lane and re-queue the rest.

KV cache strategy: tag cached KV segments with last-access epoch and lane affinity. On preemption, avoid evicting KV entries that belong to latency lane for the next 60s; instead, perform soft reclamation by trimming least-recently-used within best-effort buckets first.

Memory accounting: add transient_reservation budget per GPU to allow brief overcommit during slice transitions; track fragmentation and trigger a low-cost defragmentation sweep when reclaimed-free < threshold and no active latency lanes.
Fairness policy: implement token-bucket deficits per tenant to avoid starvation. If a tenant's deficit grows > threshold, temporarily boost them into balanced lane until deficit reduced.

Metrics: expose lane_p50/p95/p99, preemption_count, avg_preemption_latency_ms, kv_eviction_rate_by_lane, gpu_fragmentation_pct, per-tenant_deficit_score. Add alerts for preemption_count spike and kv_eviction_rate_by_lane > 20%
API/Config: runtime flag runtime.scheduler.preemptive=true, and per-account overrides: account.slo_enforcement = strict|lenient|off
Testing: unit tests for lane assignment logic, integration tests with model simulator that supports partial KV resumption, chaos tests that inject sudden latency-lane bursts
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Enable feature on 3 dedicated nodes in staging. Run synthetic mixed workload (60% best-effort token-heavy, 30% balanced, 10% latency-sensitive short requests). Validate metrics and acceptance criteria.
Phase 2 (canary): Opt-in by partner customers on Dedicated capacity (10% of cluster capacity). Monitor tail latencies and KV hit-rate for 48h. Provide quick disable if regressions observed.
Phase 3 (gradual): Gradually expand to 50% of dedicated nodes while running experiments comparing throughput and cost-per-token; run per-tenant fairness analysis and adjust deficits thresholds.
Phase 4 (general): Flip default to enabled on Dedicated and offer opt-in for Hosted API after validating multi-tenant isolation behavior
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Preemption causes KV cache churn and increases cold token cost. Mitigation: lane-affinity tagging + soft reclamation policy and retention window for latency lanes.
Risk: Throughput regression for best-effort workloads. Mitigation: deficit-based fairness throttle and throughput guardrails; ensure we can disable preemption flag at node level quickly.
Risk: Increased GPU fragmentation during partial execution. Mitigation: transient_reservation and low-cost defrag sweep plus monitoring and auto-disable if fragmentation exceeds threshold
Risk: Complexity makes debugging hard. Mitigation: add tracing hooks into scheduler decisions and sample logs for preemption events; include link to tracing dashboard in console

2026-03-06 María Alvarez (PM): Please ensure we include per-tenant observability in Console; customers must be able to see preemption events and kv hit-rate by route.
2026-03-08 Design review (Jonas Meyer): Suggested moving deficit-based fairness into separate pluggable module; also recommended keeping hard thresholds configurable per cluster.
2026-03-10 Security review: no elevated cryptographic concerns; ensure KV tagging metadata does not include PII and is stored transiently.

2026-03-11 Elliot Zhang: Integration tests created. Found an edge case where small batched requests get starved if many tiny latency requests arrive — added a fast-path that allows batching up to N_latency_small before preempting.
